pattern.crimePattern: humiliated ex-girlfriend strikes the young man who read her messages aloud at a funeral disco, during a generator blackout
pattern.notes: Fictional family and homestead. The disco matanga is shown with affection, as a community keeping a family company through the night; the crime is one person's moment, not a comment on the custom. Her messages are never shown, only described.

ob.text: Mourners report a young man, Brighton Onyiso (24), found dead behind a maize store near a funeral compound outside Siaya town at about 05:40, after the all-night funeral disco for his grandfather.

people.name: Brighton Onyiso
people.occupation: Grandson of the late Mzee Olang'
people.bio: Loud, funny, careless with people. Came home from Kisumu for the funeral.

facts.text: Brighton Onyiso was found dead behind a maize store at the funeral compound at about 05:40, after the all-night disco matanga.
One head wound. A half-smoked cigarette lies beside him in the dust.
Beside the body: small red and white glass beads, scattered, on a broken elastic.
In the long grass 30 m behind the store: a long wooden pounding pestle from the funeral kitchen.
Four sacks are missing from the store since the evening, with drag marks out of the front door to the back path. Arnold's handcart has maize dust in it.
DJ's track history: 02:10, "Brighton's request", announced on the mic. Last track before the silence: 02:38. Next track: 03:05.
Generator hire sheet: "Out of fuel about 02:40; refuelled 03:05."
Fidelis: at 01:00 Brighton took the mic and read a girl's messages out to the whole tent, laughing. The girl was Mitchelle. "It was ugly."
Fidelis: Brighton danced to his 02:10 request and stayed on the floor until the music died at 02:40, then walked off into the dark towards the store, lighting a cigarette.
Fidelis was at the generator with his boys from 02:40 to 03:05, refuelling by torchlight.
Fidelis: the family paid him in full in advance. "Nobody owes the DJ at a matanga."
Turfosa: "When the music died, I saw the girl Brighton shamed walking towards the maize store with her arms folded." One of the kitchen's long pestles was missing in the morning.
Turfosa was at her fires with three helpers all night.
Maureen: Arnold went off down the back path with a loaded handcart at about 02:35 and came back past the fires with it empty at 03:07, just after the music.
Sharleen's friends: during the blackout she held a phone torch for the DJ's boys at the generator, then danced with them when the music came back.
A printed wreath: "Rest in peace, Mzee Olang'. From your friends at Mvua Holdings." The family say he "sold land to some Nairobi company" months before he died.
Clan elders' letter: the dispute over the late Mzee's land will be settled after the burial. The parties are Arnold and his uncles. Brighton is not a party.
In Mitchelle's room: the rest of a red-and-white beaded bracelet in a dish.
Her black dress has grass seeds caught in the hem.
Autopsy: one heavy blow with a long rounded wooden object.
Autopsy: death between 02:00 and 03:30.
Autopsy: no other injuries at all; no sign of a fight, a fall or an electrical burn.
Dr. Chebii: the pestle's rounded end matches the wound.
Comparison: the scattered beads and the bracelet in Mitchelle's dish are the same beads on the same elastic; the broken ends match.
Mitchelle: "I left the disco at midnight and went home to sleep."
Mitchelle: "He was nothing to me any more."
Mitchelle admits she followed Brighton towards the store when the music stopped, "to tell him what he was".
Mitchelle: "I told him. He laughed. I walked away and he was smoking."
Arnold: "I never left the funeral tent all night."
Arnold: he took four sacks, "half mine", out of the front door at about 02:30 and went the back way to his house with his cart. He didn't see Brighton.
Sharleen: "I was at the generator holding the torch."

interrogations.intro: Mitchelle sits on a bench at the edge of the tent, her arms folded tight. "I left at midnight. I went home to sleep."
Arnold stands by the store with his hands in his pockets. "I never left the tent all night. Ask anyone."

topics.reply: The elders will settle it after the burial. That land is my father's side. Brighton had nothing to do with it.

interrogations.intro: Sharleen hasn't taken off the jacket Brighton lent her. "I don't know anyone here."

topics.reply: He read her messages. I told him to stop. He didn't. When the lights went I was holding the torch for the DJ's boys. My friends were there.

interrogations.intro: Fidelis scrolls back through the night on his laptop. "Every track has a time. Everything."
Turfosa wipes her hands on her apron by the fires. "Four hundred people, and I counted my pestles. One is gone."

contradictions.reaction: She unfolds her arms. "He read my messages to everyone. My whole village heard. I wanted to tell him what he was. That's all."
"...I took four sacks. That maize is half mine. I went the back way with my cart at about half past two and came back before the music. I didn't see Brighton."
Mitchelle looks at the beads in the evidence bag, then at her bare wrist. She doesn't say anything for a long time. "He laughed," she says at last.

events.text: Brighton reads Mitchelle's messages on the mic
events.why: The DJ: at 01:00, in front of the whole tent.
The playlist logs "Brighton's request" at 02:10; the whole tent saw him dance.
He danced until the music died at 02:40 and walked off to smoke. The music came back at 03:05. Turfosa saw Mitchelle walk to the store in the silence.
Refuelled at 03:05; the next track starts at 03:05.

decoys.why: Midnight is when Mitchelle says she left. She was in the tent at 01:00 and walking to the store at 02:40.

prosecutor.pass: The messages at one, his song at ten past two, and twenty-five minutes of silence. The playlist has a gap. That's when.
fail: Midnight is her story, not the night.
He was dancing at ten past two. When could nobody hear a thing?

prosecutor.pass: In the tent at one, walking to the store in the dark, and her bracelet in the dust beside him. That will hold.
fail: The cousin was stealing maize down the back path. He's a thief. Look again.
The new girlfriend held a torch for the DJ's boys.

prosecutor.pass: One blow with a kitchen pestle in the dark. Yes.
fail: One wound and nothing else. No fight.
A long rounded wooden object. What went missing from the kitchen?

prosecutor.pass: He read her messages to four hundred people at her neighbour's funeral. The court will understand. It will still convict.
fail: Brighton isn't a party to the land dispute.
He never went near the back path. Read the cousin's story again.

timeOfDeath.note: Dancing until the music died at 02:40; the generator came back at 03:05. The autopsy allows 02:00–03:30.

proof.concludes: Brighton was alive and dancing from 02:10 until the music died at 02:40. The only stretch when nobody could hear anything was the generator silence, 02:40 to 03:05.
Mitchelle didn't leave at midnight. At 01:00 Brighton humiliated her in front of the whole tent.
In the silence she walked to the store. The kitchen's missing pestle, from the grass behind it, matches the wound.
Her broken bracelet is beside the body. Mitchelle Aoko struck Brighton with a caterer's pounding pestle because he'd humiliated her in front of the whole funeral.

eliminations.why: Arnold was down the back path with his handcart from 02:35 until he came back past the fires at 03:07. His crime is the maize.
Sharleen held the torch at the generator through the blackout.
Fidelis was refuelling the generator with his boys.
Turfosa was at her fires with three helpers.
A single heavy blow from a long object, not a fall.
The wound is from a long rounded wooden object.
One blow and no other injuries.
Brighton isn't a party to the land dispute.
Arnold was on the back path; Brighton never went there.
The DJ was paid by the family in advance.
That would be Sharleen's, and she was at the generator.

reconstruction.text: Mzee Ezekiel Olang' dies at 81. The night before the burial the family holds a disco matanga: a tent, a DJ, a generator, food through the night.
01:00. Brighton, who left Mitchelle in November, takes the DJ's microphone, reads her messages to him aloud to the tent, and laughs.
02:10. He dances to his request. At 02:40 the generator runs dry, the music dies, and he walks off behind the maize store to smoke.
In the dark and quiet, Mitchelle takes a pestle from the kitchen and follows him. She strikes him once. Her bracelet snaps.
She throws the pestle into the grass. At 03:05 the music comes back and the tent dances on. At noon the family were to bury their grandfather.

clockPlan.note: No detention needed. One warrant on her room. Every comparison is immediate.

glossary.def: A funeral, and the days of mourning before the burial.
An all-night funeral disco to keep the bereaved family company and raise money for the funeral.
A long wooden pestle for pounding grain.
A farm or plot of land.
Respectful word for an older man.

ui.beatNotes: A playlist as a clock. The DJ's track history drops onto the rail as a ribbon of song titles; the generator silence shows as a gap you can see, and the event cards snap into it.
